heroHeadline: FIFA Confirms Infantino Will Seek Fourth Term as UEFA Hunts for a Challenger
heroSubtitle: FIFA officially confirmed Sep 6 that embattled president Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election at the March 18, 2027 Congress in Rabat, a spokesperson saying 'nothing has changed' since he first signaled his intent in April. The confirmation lands amid an unresolved standoff with UEFA over his abandoned $4.2 billion World Cup stake-sale plan: FIFA moved from defense to offense Sep 3-4, filing a Colorado federal court motion accusing UEFA's discovery requests — pursued in three US courts, including one targeting Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital — of being 'little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign.' No formal challenger to Infantino has yet declared ahead of the Nov 18 candidacy deadline; UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin says he is seeking a single viable candidate, with CONCACAF's Victor Montagliani widely viewed as the front-runner alongside AFC president Sheikh Salman. Kushner gave his most extensive comments yet in a Sep 4 Fortune interview, saying Thrive 'would not have gotten involved' had it foreseen the fallout, while Infantino himself dodged questions about his future at the U20 Women's World Cup opening in Poland on Sep 5.
